title: ci: drop external DTD from minimal fontconfig to avoid expat NULL-deref crash
body:
## What

Removes the external DTD declaration from the minimal fontconfig config that the Linux smoke-test job installs as a workaround for the expat 2.6.1 NULL-deref CVEs.

```diff
  <?xml version="1.0"?>
- <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
  <fontconfig>
```

## Why

The job already sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE=/tmp/fonts-minimal.conf` with `<include>` removed to avoid the expat external-entity crash path. But a flaky smoke-test failure ([run 28140700565](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/28140700565/job/83337233535), `Linux / Electron-Smoke`) still crashed with that workaround active.

I pulled the crash-dump artifact and walked the minidump. The faulting thread was a **SIGSEGV (NULL deref, fault address 0x0)** with this native stack:

```
libc.so.6
libfontconfig.so.1   (config parsing)
libexpat.so.1        (XML / external-entity parsing)
...Chromium browser-process font-init frames...
```

i.e. the crash is in **libexpat called from libfontconfig during Chromium's browser-process font initialization at startup** — not in VS Code/Chromium logic. The dump confirms `FONTCONFIG_FILE=/tmp/fonts-minimal.conf` was in effect and the minimal config was loaded.

The remaining trigger is the `<!DOCTYPE … SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">` line: fontconfig feeds that DTD to expat as an external **parameter** entity, which still hits the not-yet-backported `CVE-2026-32776` / `CVE-2026-32778` NULL-deref paths on expat 2.6.1 even after `<include>` was removed. fontconfig does not require the DOCTYPE, so dropping it removes the last external-entity codepath.

## Validation

- Workflow YAML parses (PyYAML `safe_load`).
- The generated config (DOCTYPE removed) parses as valid XML; the diagnostics step's `ElementTree.parse` does not fetch external DTDs, so it is unaffected.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is a mitigation. The durable fix is shipping `libexpat >= 2.7.5` on the runner; the step already auto-disables the whole workaround when it detects that version.
- Companion harness PR #322905 makes such a launch crash fail fast with an actionable error instead of a 120s opaque Mocha `before all` hook timeout.

title: editor: show editor layout actions in single tab mode
body:
## What

`SingleEditorTabsControl.prepareEditorLayoutActions` now returns the resolved editor layout actions instead of an empty set.

## Why

The Agents (sessions) window contributes its editor-area layout controls — **Maximize Editor Area**, **Restore Editor Area**, **Close Editor Area**, **Open in Modal Editor**, and the secondary side bar toggle — to the `MenuId.EditorTitleLayout` menu.

That menu is rendered by the editor tabs control. When `workbench.editor.showTabs` is set to `single`, the active control is `SingleEditorTabsControl`, which overrode `prepareEditorLayoutActions()` to always return empty actions. As a result, the Maximize Editor option (and the rest of the layout group) disappeared in single-tab mode.

## Notes for reviewers

This has **no visible effect on the regular VS Code editor window**:

- `MenuId.EditorTitleLayout` is only populated by the Agents window (`src/vs/sessions/`); there are no core or extension contributions to it.
- Extensions cannot target it — the extension menu contribution points expose only `editor/title`, the modal editor title, and `editor/title/run`.
- When the menu is empty, the layout toolbar renders nothing and its separator is explicitly hidden.

So in the standard workbench this is effectively a no-op, while the Agents window now shows the Maximize/Restore/Close/Modal layout actions even with `showTabs: single`.

title: smoke: fail fast with actionable error when Electron crashes during launch
body:
## What

The per-suite `before all` hook in the Electron smoke tests launches Electron via Playwright's `_electron.launch`. It was called with `timeout: 0` (no timeout), and the first-window wait used `timeout: 0` too.

This PR gives both the launch and the first-window wait a finite timeout (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT = 60s`, well below Mocha's 120s `before all` hook timeout) and wraps them so a failure is re-thrown as an actionable error that points at the crash-dump directory and the Playwright trace.

## Why

Investigating a flaky smoke-test failure ([run 28140700565](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/28140700565/job/83337233535), `Linux / Electron-Smoke`):

```
1) VSCode Smoke Tests (Electron)
     Search
       "before all" hook for "verifies the sidebar moves to the right":
     Error: Timeout of 120000ms exceeded.
```

Root cause from the artifacts:

- The `before all` hook started `playwright-electron#launch` and then went completely silent for 120s (no Electron stdout at all), while the next suite launched normally in ~800ms.
- The crash-dump artifact contains a minidump for the `8_suite_Search` launch (`pending/…dmp`), timestamped ~1s after the launch was spawned: **SIGSEGV** (exception code `0xb`) in the Electron main/browser process, in the Chromium sandbox startup path (`sandbox_ipc_linux.cc`, `network_sandbox.cc`, `namespace_sandbox.cc`).

Because `_electron.launch` was called with `timeout: 0`, the crash never surfaced as a launch failure — the promise just hung until Mocha killed the hook at 120s, producing an opaque timeout with no hint that a native crash had occurred. This also explains why the same 120000ms timeout shows up across many different suites' `before all` hooks: the underlying native launch crash is suite-independent and rare, so it lands on whichever suite happens to be starting.

## Notes for reviewers

- This makes the harness fail **fast** (~60s instead of 120s) and **diagnosably** (error message references the crash-dump dir + trace). It does not add a launch retry — that can be a follow-up.
- The underlying Electron/Chromium startup crash itself is being investigated separately; this PR is about no longer masking it behind a generic Mocha hook timeout.
- Could not run the repo hygiene/compile tasks locally (node_modules not installed in this worktree); the change is isolated to `test/automation` and was transpile-checked in isolation.

title: Embed native RDP / external application windows inside VS Code editor tabs
body:
Type: Feature Request ## Feature Request: Allow extensions to embed native remote desktop sessions inside an editor tab ### Summary I would like VS Code to support embedding a native Remote Desktop / RDP session directly inside an editor tab, in the same area where files such as `runTest.js` are displayed. Currently, VS Code extensions can open Webviews, terminals, custom editors, and external applications, but there does not seem to be an official API that allows an extension to host a native OS window, such as `mstsc.exe`, inside a VS Code editor tab. ### Use case I am building a VS Code extension for remote development and automation. The goal is to let users manage SSH, macros, terminal automation, and remote desktop connections from a single VS Code workspace. A useful workflow would be: 1. Open VS Code. 2. Select a saved remote machine. 3. Open an RDP session. 4. Display the remote desktop directly inside a VS Code editor tab, next to source files, terminals, and extension views. This would make VS Code a unified remote operations workspace rather than forcing users to switch between VS Code and a separate Remote Desktop window. ### Current limitations At the moment, the available options are: * Launch `mstsc.exe` or another RDP client externally. * Use a Webview with an HTML5 remote desktop gateway such as Apache Guacamole. * Open a browser-based remote desktop interface inside VS Code’s Simple Browser or a custom Webview. These workarounds are useful, but they are not equivalent to embedding a native RDP client directly in VS Code. Launching an external RDP client breaks the integrated workflow, while using a web gateway requires extra infrastructure and is more complex for users to install. ### Requested capability It would be helpful if VS Code provided an official API that allows extensions to embed or host native external application windows inside an editor tab or custom editor. For example, an extension could start a process such as: ```text mstsc.exe ``` and attach its window to a VS Code editor area. A possible API could look conceptually like: ```ts vscode.window.createNativeWindowPanel({ title: 'Remote Desktop', executable: 'mstsc.exe', args: ['connection.rdp'], viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.One }); ``` This does not need to be specific to RDP. The general capability would be useful for tools that need to display native UI inside VS Code while remaining part of the workspace. ### Security considerations I understand that embedding native windows inside VS Code may have security, portability, and sandboxing implications. A safe version of this feature could include: * Explicit user confirmation before launching or embedding a native application. * Workspace Trust restrictions. * Extension permission declarations. * Platform-specific support only where feasible. * Clear separation between Webviews and native embedded windows. * No automatic access to credentials or system resources beyond the launched process. ### Why this would be valuable This would enable extensions to provide a much more integrated experience for: * Remote desktop / RDP tools. * VM consoles. * Embedded device consoles. * Legacy enterprise tools. * Remote administration workflows. * Development environments that require both code and graphical remote access. For users, the benefit would be a single VS Code workspace containing code, terminals, logs, automation tools, and remote desktop sessions. ### Alternative If embedding arbitrary native windows is not feasible, another useful option would be an official remote desktop view API or a recommended extension API pattern for building integrated RDP/VNC/remote display clients inside VS Code. Thank you for considering this feature request. Currently, when using the GitHub Copilot chat interface, each coding agent's answer concludes with a small string of metadata/statistics, such as:

### ➕ Describe the solution you'd like

I would love to see the total duration of the generation—measured from the exact moment the prompt is submitted to when the response completes—appended to that same stats line.

* `MAI-Code-1-Flash • 2.5 credits • 0:03`

The only current alternative is manually tracking the clock or opening developer tools to inspect network request timings, both of which are cumbersome for standard daily use.

* This will help developers better evaluate model performance and responsiveness directly within their workflow.

Claude Code is configured in our enterprise environment to use Anthropic models through Amazon Bedrock and works correctly when used directly.

However, when attempting to use the Claude Agent from GitHub Copilot Chat, the agent consistently fails during execution. The same issue occurs in both WSL and native Windows environments, which suggests this is not specific to WSL.

The main difficulty is that the failure does not expose enough diagnostic information to determine whether the issue originates from:

* GitHub Copilot Chat
* Claude Agent integration
* Claude Code
* Amazon Bedrock
* Authentication/authorization

Claude Agent should successfully execute using the same enterprise Claude model configuration that Claude Code uses.

The agent fails during execution. The surfaced error information is insufficient to identify the root cause or determine which component is failing.

  * Whether model invocation succeeds

title: build: keep Linux smoke test data off the small OS root disk
body:
## Problem

The **Linux (X64)** smoke test steps intermittently exhaust the agent's **OS root disk**. When `/` fills, the Azure agent **worker** itself crashes while writing its own diagnostic log:

```
##[error]Unhandled exception. System.IO.IOException: No space left on device : '/usr/local/vss-agent/4.274.1/_diag/Worker_*.log'
```

Because the worker dies mid-step (not the test), the job can't cancel cleanly and **hangs until timeout** — i.e. the step appears to "run forever", while the other OS legs are fine. Example: [run 20260625.13 (insider)](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=450828&view=logs&j=dcea01d9-8513-5a47-c936-5baceabd8c97), step "🧪 Run smoke tests (Electron)". This is the same recurring "Linux out of space" class of failure seen previously on the `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64` pool.

## Root cause

Smoke **logs** and **crashes** already live under `.build/` on the large work volume (`/mnt/...`), so they're fine. But the smoke **data dir** is rooted at `os.tmpdir()`:

```ts
// test/smoke/src/main.ts
const testDataPath = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `vscsmoke-${getTestTypeSuffix()}`);
```

On the Linux agents `os.tmpdir()` resolves to `/tmp` on the **small OS root disk**, and `testDataPath` holds the user-data dir, extensions dir, workspace, the copied stable build, and — newly significant — the **Copilot CLI / agent-host session state** (`XDG_STATE_HOME` is pinned under the per-run `userDataDir`). The chat-session smoke tests spawn real Copilot CLI / Claude / Codex SDK processes, so this directory can grow large during the run and tip the small disk over.

## Fix (mitigation)

- Point `TMPDIR` at `$(Agent.TempDirectory)` (on the large work volume) for the **Electron**, **Browser** and **Remote** smoke steps, so `os.tmpdir()`/`testDataPath` no longer lands on `/`. Node's `os.tmpdir()` honours `$TMPDIR`, and the smoke harness's own setup/teardown rimraf of `testDataPath` continues to work unchanged.
- Add `df -h` to the **before/after** diagnostics steps and dump the smoke data dir sizes afterwards, so the next occurrence of disk pressure is immediately visible (which mount, which dir).

This is a mitigation that lives in this repo and unblocks CI now. The **proper fix is infrastructure**: increase the OS-disk size / SKU of the `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64` 1ES hosted pool — that has to be requested from the pool owner / 1ES team and is tracked separately.

## Notes / validation
- YAML validated locally (`js-yaml` load OK); passes repo hygiene precommit.
- Assumption: `$(Agent.TempDirectory)` is on the same large volume as `_work` (`/mnt/...`) on these agents — the new `df -h` output will confirm this in the first run.

title: Fixes Remote-SSH Windows to Linux .mcp.json error ENOENT
body:
This is a proposed fix for #320167

Currently the code resolves the home directory on the client side and sends it to `spawn()` as `cwd`. When connected to a Linux remote, the Windows cwd (with backslashes) generates the `ENOENT` error when attempting to start any MCP server from `.mcp.json`.

This change sets the initial cwd as undefined and then resolves cwd on the remote side via `roots?.[0]`. I reviewed the MCP specs [here](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) and [here](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25) and they don't explicitly define the cwd w.r.t. mcp servers that may contain relative paths, though resolving cwd to project root is consistent with `.vscode/mcp.json`.

I added a basic regression test but I welcome suggestions or improvements.

~~Also, I was not able to fully confirm this fixes the issue in my local build because the Remote-SSH extension does not run on local builds ("Remote - SSH is only supported in Microsoft versions of VS Code"). Would love if someone able to create an official build is able to pick this up and test it out. Thanks!~~

**Update 6/26/26** - I was able to test this by having Copilot apply a JS bundle patch version of this PR to my live VS Code instance instead of trying to re-build from scratch with the fix (Remote-SSH doesn't allow this). With the patch applied, I confirmed that VS Code with Remote-SSH is able to connect to MCP servers in `.mcp.json` without generating the `ENOENT` error. I reviewed the JS patch line-by-line to confirm it reflects the code changes in this PR (happy to provide details if requested. thanks!

title: fix: Add selection to next Find match does not work with Regex Find Mode
body:
## Summary

The "Add Selection to Next Find Match" (Ctrl+D) feature is implemented by `MultiCursorSession` in `src/vs/editor/contrib/multicursor/browser/multicursor.ts`. When the find widget owns the search (focus is in the find widget, the widget is revealed, and the search string is non-empty), the session uses the find...


## Root cause

The "Add Selection to Next Find Match" (Ctrl+D) feature is implemented by
`MultiCursorSession` in `src/vs/editor/contrib/multicursor/browser/multicursor.ts`.

When the find widget owns the search (focus is in the find widget, the widget is
revealed, and the search string is non-empty), the session uses the find widget's
search string and its `wholeWord` / `matchCase` options. However, the model lookups
in `_getNextMatch`, `_getPreviousMatch`, and `selectAll` all passed the `isRegex`
argument to `findNextMatch` / `findPreviousMatch` / `findMatches` as a hardcoded
`false`. As a result, a regex pattern coming from the find widget was always treated
as literal text, so no further matches were found and no cursor was added.


## What changed

File: `src/vs/editor/contrib/multicursor/browser/multicursor.ts`

- Added an `isRegex` field to `MultiCursorSession` (constructor parameter).
- In `MultiCursorSession.create`, pass `findState.isRegex` when the find widget owns
 the search, and `false` for the selection-owned case (the search text there is the
 literal selected text, so regex must stay off, which also matches the existing
 `isRegexOverride: FindOptionOverride.False` behavior for the disconnected case).
- Replaced the hardcoded `false` isRegex argument with `this.isRegex` in the
 `findNextMatch`, `findPreviousMatch`, and the two `findMatches` calls.

File: `src/vs/editor/contrib/multicursor/test/browser/multicursor.test.ts`

- Added a regression test "AddSelectionToNextFindMatchAction works with regex find
 mode (#107090)" that turns on regex mode in the find controller with pattern `a.c`
 and verifies that each `Ctrl+D` adds the next regex match as a new selection.


## Issue

Fixes #107090

Issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/107090

## Testing


- Ran the relevant tests and linter for the changed files while developing.

## Description

Investigated whether `unhandlederror-GitHubLoginFailed` (#321639) is the same error addressed by #321956 and would be fixed by it. Conclusion: **no** — they are two distinct errors in different layers. No code change is warranted in this repository.

### Findings

- **This issue (#321639)** — `GitHubLoginFailedError` (extends `ErrorNoTelemetry`) thrown by `_authShowWarnings` in the **Copilot Chat extension**: `extensions/copilot/src/platform/authentication/vscode-node/copilotTokenManager.ts:136`, when no GitHub session is found. Matches the reported frame `xie._authShowWarnings (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js)`.
- **#321956 / #321950** — `ProtocolError(AHP_AUTH_REQUIRED)` (code `-32007`, message "Authentication is required to use Copilot") re-raised by a `catch`-less `void promise.finally(...)` cleanup chain in **core**: `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/agentSubscription.ts` (`trackSessionCreate`).
- The two differ in error type, message, telemetry bucket, and originating layer. #321956 modifies only `agentSubscription.ts` and never touches the extension's token-fetch path, so it cannot fix #321639.

### Why no code change here

The throw site lives in `extensions/copilot/`, the vendored build of the Copilot Chat extension (synced from `microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat`). A fix for the `GitHubLoginFailed` unhandled-error path belongs upstream, not in this clone.

### Recommendation

Keep #321639 separate from #321956; route the `GitHubLoginFailed` fix to `microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat`.

title: agentHost: fix subagent transcript replay + bump Claude/Codex SDKs
body:
Three related changes to the agent host, grouped because the SDK bump and the replay fix were validated together.

## 1. Replay mapper: reconstruct prompt-less subagent transcripts (the bug)

`ReplayBuilder` in `claudeReplayMapper.ts` only opens a turn on a `user-text` message and drops any assistant message that arrives with no active turn. A subagent transcript returned by `getSubagentMessages` carries a `parent_tool_use_id` on every envelope and has **no synthetic spawning prompt**, so it opens directly with an assistant message. As a result every inner assistant message — including the subagent's final reply — was dropped and the subagent transcript reconstructed as **zero turns** on reopen (the `getSubagentMessages` call returned the real messages, but `mapSessionMessagesToTurns` produced 0 turns).

**Fix:** thread an `isInner` flag (set when `parent_tool_use_id !== null`) through the parsed assistant message. When there is no active turn:
- **inner (subagent) message** → synthesize an empty-prompt turn to hold the reply, then process its blocks normally;
- **top-level message** → keep the existing drop-with-warn (genuinely anomalous).

Scoped strictly to subagent transcripts; top-level replay is unchanged. Adds unit fixtures for the prompt-less subagent shape (*Fixture 10*) and the unchanged top-level drop (*Fixture 10b*).

## 2. Bump Claude (0.3.187) and Codex (0.142.0) SDKs

Updates `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` → `0.3.187` and `@openai/codex` → `0.142.0` (root `package.json` + lockfile and both `build/agent-sdk` tarball pins). The new Claude SDK adds `setMcpPermissionModeOverride` to the `Query` interface, so the `Query` test doubles are updated to satisfy it: `ImmediatelyDoneQuery` (and the `RecordingQuery` that extends it), `FakeQuery`, and `RoundTripQuery`.

## 3. Enable the Codex provider in the real-SDK test server

`startRealServer` forwarded `--codex-sdk-root` but never set the Codex enable flag, and the Codex agent defaults to disabled — so the provider never registered and every Codex real-SDK test failed with `No agent provider registered for: codex`. The fork now sets `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_CODEX_AGENT_ENABLED` when a codex SDK root is supplied.

## Testing

Validated against current `main`:

- **Unit** (`claudeReplayMapper`): 12 passing, incl. Fixtures 10 / 10b.
- **Real-SDK integration** (`AGENT_HOST_REAL_SDK=1` / `AGENT_HOST_REAL_CODEX=1`):
  - **Claude** `reopening a session keeps sub-agent messages out of the parent transcript (replay path)` — passes (previously reconstructed the subagent transcript empty).
  - **Copilot** same shared replay test — passes.
  - **Codex** full suite — 13 passing (provider now registers).
- Verified live in the authenticated Agents window: reopening a persisted subagent session reconstructs the nested subagent transcript, and the parent transcript does not leak the subagent's content.

## Note

The real-SDK replay test harness itself was repaired separately on `main` in #322837 (chat-channel filter + complete approval action), which is what surfaced the product bug fixed here.

title: Persist multi-root folder picker choice to new agent-host chats
body:
Fixes #321453

## Problem

For agent-host (AHP) chat sessions in the editor in a multi-root workspace: pick a folder in the Folder picker, send a message, then click **New chat** — the picker resets to the first folder instead of remembering your choice.

## Root cause

The chosen working folder is stored in `AgentHostNewSessionFolderService`, **keyed by the session's untitled compose resource**. Clicking *New chat* mints a *new* compose resource, so `getFolder(newResource)` returns `undefined` and every working-directory resolution site falls back to `workspace.folders[0]`.

## Fix

Add a window-level **sticky default folder** to `IAgentHostNewSessionFolderService`:

- `setFolder` records the latest choice as the default.
- New `getDefaultFolder()` returns it, validated against the current workspace folders (a folder removed from the workspace is dropped).
- It is intentionally **not** cleared on session disposal, so it persists across new chats for the window's lifetime.

All resolution sites now fall back to `getDefaultFolder()` before `folders[0]` — both the *display* sites (picker, working-dir chip / provisional) and the *actual cwd* sites (materialization in the list controller + the session handler) — so the picker and the session the new chat actually runs in stay consistent.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✓
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✓
- Unit tests: folder-service suite (2 new tests) ✓ and full `AgentHost` suite (1081 passing) ✓, including the existing multi-root folder-picker tests.

Prepares `chat.agentHost.enabled` for progressive (TAS-cohorted) rollout to Stable, without regressing Insiders' default-on behavior or other in-flight experiments on related editor/Agents-window settings.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8185

## What changed

**1. Add a TAS hook to the setting** — `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHost.config.contribution.ts`
- Added `experiment: { mode: 'startup' }` to `chat.agentHost.enabled`. The `default` (`!isWeb && product.quality !== 'stable'`) and `tags` are unchanged.
- This is non-disruptive: `processExperimentalSettings` only registers an override when the treatment value differs from `schema.default`. So Insiders (static default `true`) see a no-op, while a Stable cohort (static default `false`) can be flipped on by a `true` treatment. The default treatment name resolves to `config.chat.agentHost.enabled`.
- The browser-layer policy file already spreads `...existingProp`, so the new `experiment` block flows into the policy-augmented re-registration with no change there.

**2. Close the main-process spawn gap** — `src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts`
- Always instantiate `ElectronAgentHostStarter` + `AgentHostProcessManager` (removed the `if (isAgentHostEnabled(...))` guard and the now-unused import).

Previously a cohorted Stable user's renderer would think the agent host is on while the main process never registered the `vscode:createAgentHostMessageChannel` IPC listener — so nothing spawned.

- Precommit hygiene — passed

title: Gate Claude3PIntegration behind editor preview policy
body:
## Problem

The `Claude3PIntegration` enterprise policy was **owned by the copilot-chat extension setting** `github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled` via the distro `product.json` `extensionConfigurationPolicy` block. Because `product.json` is pure JSON, that owner cannot carry a `value(policyData)` callback, so the policy only responded to OS/MDM admin policy and **never honored the account-side preview-features flag** `chat_preview_features_enabled` (sourced from the Copilot token's `editor_preview_features`).

By contrast, **Codex works**: its core setting `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled` owns `Codex3PIntegration` in code with a `value` callback gating on `chat_preview_features_enabled`.

## Fix — flip ownership (mirror Codex)

- The in-code core setting `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` now **owns** `Claude3PIntegration` with the preview-features `value` callback.
- The extension setting `github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled` attaches via a **`policyReference`** declared from `product.json`.

## `extensionConfigurationPolicy` now supports both forms

An `extensionConfigurationPolicy` entry can be **either**:

1. **Owner / "parent" syntax** (existing, unchanged) — the setting owns the policy inline:
   ```json
   "github.copilot.nextEditSuggestions.enabled": {
       "name": "CopilotNextEditSuggestions",
       "category": "InteractiveSession",
       "minimumVersion": "1.99",
       "description": "…"
   }
   ```
2. **Reference syntax** (new) — the setting attaches to a policy owned by an in-code setting, mirroring the in-code `policyReference` configuration field:
   ```json
   "github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled": {
       "policyReference": { "name": "Claude3PIntegration" }
   }
   ```

`configurationExtensionPoint` and the policy exporter detect the `policyReference` key to route an entry to `.policy` vs `.policyReference`. The exporter links reference entries into the owner's `referencedSettings` and skips type validation for settings not registered in the headless export process.

Implementation:

- New `IExtensionConfigurationPolicyReference` type; `extensionConfigurationPolicy` widened to `IStringDictionary<IPolicy | IExtensionConfigurationPolicyReference>`.
- Regenerates `policyData.jsonc` and updates the export test fixture.

## Net effect

- The admin `Claude3PIntegration` ADMX/plist is still generated (now from the in-code owner).
- Preview-features gating now applies to **both** the editor surface (`github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled`) and the agent-host surface (`chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled`).

## Distro change (merged)

The companion distro change — microsoft/vscode-distro#1434, which turns the claude `extensionConfigurationPolicy` entry into a `policyReference` — has **merged to `main`**. This PR bumps `package.json` `"distro"` to `7abf39b86c07d094722a4b3ec9f37e78fe3d5db3` to pick it up, so it is now self-contained.

## Validation

Verified end-to-end via the Policy Inspector diagnostics:

- With the account's `editor_preview_features_enabled: false` (→ `chat_preview_features_enabled: false`), **both** `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` and `github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled` resolve to `false` via **AccountPolicyService** — i.e. the account-side preview-features flag is now honored (the original bug), matching Codex.
- A native **MDM** policy (`CopilotNextEditSuggestions`, an owner-syntax `extensionConfigurationPolicy` entry) still applies via `PolicyChannelClient`, confirming the existing owner path is **not regressed** and both forms coexist.

title: Voice mode: add send keyword for hands-free submit
body:
Users can now configure a keyword phrase (e.g. "send it") via the new `agents.voice.sendKeyword` setting. When the keyword is detected at the end of the spoken transcript, it is stripped from the message and the request is submitted automatically.

This enables a fully hands-free workflow without relying on silence-based auto-send.

- On each transcription event, if in toggle mode with auto-send disabled, check if transcript ends with the keyword (case-insensitive)
- If matched: strip the keyword, update the transcript display, trigger send

title: sessions: Close, reopen, and delete chats in the agents window session view
body:
---
## What

Adds the ability to **close**, **reopen**, and **delete** chats in the Agents window session view.

- **Close a chat** — the tab's close (x) button now *hides* the chat from the tab strip instead of deleting it. Closed chats are preserved and can be reopened.
- **Reopen a chat** — the session header has a **Conversations** dropdown (a registered submenu) listing every chat in the session with a checkbox: checked chats are shown as tabs, unchecked chats are closed (hidden). Toggling an entry closes or reopens the corresponding chat. It also offers a **New Chat** entry.
- **Delete a chat** — permanent removal moved to an explicit **Delete Chat** action in the tab context menu (destructive). The main chat cannot be closed or deleted; it lives and dies with its session.

## How

- `IActiveSession` gains two read-only view-state observables: `openChats` (chats shown as tabs) and `closedChats` (hidden but reopenable). Closing/reopening is a *view* operation driven through the sessions (view) service, not a mutation on the session itself — mirroring `sticky`.
- `closeChat` / `openChat` mutators added to the sessions service and the `VisibleSessions` view-state layer. Closed-chat URIs are persisted in the session-state DTO so the hidden/closed state survives reloads.
- The tab strip now renders `openChats` rather than all chats.
- The **Conversations** dropdown is a registered submenu (`Menus.SessionConversations`). Because `Menus.SessionBarToolbar` is rendered once per visible session view (header/floating toolbar) with its own scoped context, the submenu is scoped per-session via a new `sessionId` context key (`equals` clause) and executes against the forwarded toolbar context — so each header operates on its own chats in a multi-session grid.

- Closed-chat resources are persisted as `string[]` in the JSON-serialized session-state DTO (consistent with the sibling `sessionResource` / `activeChatResource` fields), not `URI[]`.

title: agentHost: ignore subagent mode changes so the session mode picker doesn't reset to Plan
body:
Fixes #321960

## Problem

Asking a question in **Interactive** mode and returning to a session showed the chat input in **Plan** mode after the agent did some edits.

## Root cause

The Copilot SDK's `session.mode_changed` event carries an optional `agentId` field. Per the SDK type, it is *"absent for events from the root/main agent and session-level events"* — so a present `agentId` means the event originated from a **sub-agent** (e.g. a `task` tool sub-agent, which commonly runs in plan mode).

`CopilotAgentSession`'s `onSessionModeChanged` handler synced every `mode_changed` event into the **session-level** AHP config (`SessionConfigKey.Mode`), which drives the chat input mode picker — without checking `agentId`, unlike all the other sub-agent event handlers in the file. So when the model (running interactively) spawned a sub-agent during edits, the sub-agent's internal mode change leaked into the root session config and flipped the picker to **Plan**.

## Fix

Ignore `session.mode_changed` events that carry an `agentId`, so only root/session-level mode changes update the shared session config. This mirrors the existing sub-agent event-routing conventions in the same file.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.
- Added a regression test (`session.mode_changed from a subagent does not update the session config`).
- All 146 tests in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` pass, including the existing root-level mode-change tests.

title: chat: make Send Immediately work for agent-host sessions
body:
## Problem

The "Send Immediately" button is a no-op for agent-host managed sessions.

The action does three things:
1. Reorders the target message to the front of the queue
2. Cancels the current request (`ChatTurnCancelled`)
3. Calls `processPendingRequests` to start the next message

**Root cause:** `ChatService.processNextPendingRequest` short-circuits for agent-host sessions (`_isServerManagedQueue`), because those sessions normally let the *server* drain the queue. But the server only auto-drains on **natural turn completion** (`_runTurnCompleteSideEffects` runs on `ChatTurnComplete`), **not on cancellation** (`ChatTurnCancelled` just marks the turn cancelled). So after "Send Immediately" cancels the active turn, neither the server nor the client started the next message — the queued message just sat there.

## Fix

Added a `force` parameter that lets the explicit "Send Immediately" path bypass the server-managed-queue short-circuit, so the client dequeues and sends the next request itself (via the normal `_sendRequestAsync` → `_handleTurn` path, which dispatches a fresh `ChatTurnStarted`; `_syncPendingMessages` removes the message from the server queue). The automatic `.finally()` drain path keeps its no-op behavior for agent-host sessions, avoiding double-processing.

## Changes
- `chatService.ts` — `processPendingRequests(sessionResource, force?)` interface + doc
- `chatServiceImpl.ts` — thread `force` through to `processNextPendingRequest`, gate the guard on `!force`
- `chatQueueActions.ts` — `ChatSendPendingImmediatelyAction` now passes `force = true`
- `mockChatService.ts` — signature update
- `chatService.test.ts` — regression test for an `agent-host-copilot` session

## Validation
- Typecheck passes
- All 50 ChatService unit tests pass

title: agent host: model client connection state as a discriminated union
body:
## Summary

Refactors `IClientRecord` in `ProtocolServerHandler` into a discriminated union so the core liveness invariant is enforced by the type system rather than by convention.

Previously a single record shape carried `connections`, `lastSeenAt`, and `disconnectTimeouts` together, with an unwritten rule that **a record holding live connections must never hold armed tool-call disconnect-grace timers**. A reconnect that pushed a transport without disposing those timers could violate that rule, leaving a grace timer armed against a client that is actually connected.

This makes the bad state unrepresentable:

- **`IActiveClientRecord`** (`state: 'active'`) — one or more live transports, never any grace timers.
- **`IGraceClientRecord`** (`state: 'grace'`) — no transport, may hold armed timers, with a non-optional `lastSeenAt`.

Transitions are funneled through two places:
- **`_attachConnection` (→ active)** — promoting a grace record disposes its disconnect timers (the grace window only applies while the client has no live transport).
- **transport `onClose` (→ grace)** — demotes once the last transport is gone and arms the grace timer.

All record access now branches on `state`, so callers — including the recently added reconnect-reconciliation path (`_reconcileActiveClientsAfterReconnect`) — can no longer read `connections` off a disconnected record by accident.

### Background

This came out of investigating dogfood reports of the browser tools failing with `Client <id> disconnected before completing <tool>` against live clients. The disconnect-grace machinery has since been reworked upstream (multiple active clients per session, reconnect reconciliation, subscription filtering); this change is the type-safety hardening of that area and is **behaviour-preserving** on top of it.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- Hygiene ✅
- Full `ProtocolServerHandler` suite (66 tests) passes unchanged — genuine-disconnect, overlapping-transport, never-connected, orphaned-stamp, and reconnect cases.

title: agentHost: implement Claude session fork (Phase 6.5)
body:
## Phase 6.5 — Claude session fork

Implements `ClaudeAgent.createSession({ fork })`, replacing the `TODO: Phase 6.5` throw. This wires up the Agents-window "Fork conversation from this point" affordance for Claude sessions (which is Claude's only "truncate-by-fork" path — Claude has no in-place `truncateSession`).

### What it does
- Translates the protocol `turnId` → the SDK envelope `uuid` of that turn's **last assistant message** by walking the source transcript on demand (`resolveForkAnchorUuid`, co-located with the replay mapper so it shares the exact turn-boundary rule — no parser drift).
- Calls a new `forkSession` SDK binding with `upToMessageId` (INCLUSIVE, keep `[0..N]`).
- Inherits the source overlay (`model` / `permissionMode` / `agent`; **not** `customizationDirectory`, which is per-session and re-synced).
- `config.fork.turnIdMapping` is a no-op for Claude — `forkSession` already remaps every internal uuid and Claude keeps no per-turn event-id DB.

### Lifecycle (CONTEXT M9)
Fork writes the forked session file but does **not** start the SDK `Query`. Materialization is deferred to the first `sendMessage`, which resumes from disk. This avoids firing `onDidMaterializeSession` and pipeline progress signals before `AgentService.createSession` registers the (non-provisional) forked session — both of which otherwise produced `unknown session` warnings. This matches Copilot, whose resume path likewise never fires the materialize event. *(This was the original eager-materialize design corrected during the live E2E — see the plan's Drift section.)*

### Verification
- **171** unit/integration tests green; `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, and ESLint clean.
- **Live E2E** (fork-and-continue): 3-turn Claude session → fork at the middle turn → new session with the kept prefix and the dropped tail → new turn lands via `Options.resume` → survives an agent-host restart (fork ✕ Phase 13 replay). Both `unknown session` warnings verified at count 0. Forked-session `cwd` survives the fork.

### Files
- `claudeReplayMapper.ts` — new exported `resolveForkAnchorUuid`.
- `claudeAgentSdkService.ts` — new `forkSession` binding.
- `claudeAgent.ts` — `_forkSession` flow (deferred materialization).
- `roadmap.md` / `phase6.5-plan.md` — marked done + retrospective.

title: sessions: responsive auto-collapse of the sessions sidebar (D7)
body:
## What

Adds a responsive layout behaviour (**D7**) to the desktop Agents window: on a **narrow** window (main container ≤ 1800px) the **sessions sidebar** is automatically hidden while **both** the editor and the side panel (auxiliary bar) are open, and shown again as soon as either of them closes or the window grows wide again.

- A **manual** sidebar close is remembered — auto-show is suppressed until the user opens it again.
- Suspended while the editor is **maximized** (D5) and while **multiple sessions** are visible.
- Gated by a new experimental setting `sessions.layout.autoCollapseSessionsSidebar`, default **on** in non-stable builds (Insiders / exploration), **off** in stable.

## Why

On laptop-sized windows the sidebar, editor, and side panel compete for a cramped horizontal layout. Auto-collapsing the sidebar when the other two are open keeps the working area usable without forcing the user to manage it manually.

## Navigation must never auto-hide the sidebar

Switching sessions restores layout through **two async paths** that reveal parts in a *later* autorun run:

1. the desktop aux-bar restore (`openView` / `openViewContainer`), and
2. the base controller's editor working-set apply (`_applyWorkingSet`, which reveals the editor part **after an `await`** and runs on a `Sequencer` microtask).

An inline "same-run session changed" check only absorbed the synchronous transition, so the async editor reveal still auto-hid the sidebar on navigation. The fix moves a shared restore epoch into the **base** controller (`_withSessionLayoutRestore` / `_isRestoringSessionLayout`) and wraps **both** restore paths; the D7 autorun re-baselines instead of reacting while a restore is in flight.

Notes for reviewers:
- The epoch is a **depth counter**, not a boolean, because a single switch starts two independent restores whose promises settle in independent order (and consecutive switches can overlap). The guard must stay up until the *last* restore settles.
- The helper decrements **synchronously** for void/sync work and only defers for real Promises — otherwise a no-op restore (e.g. a session with no workspace, which also runs on construction) would leave the flag stuck `true`.

## Refactor

Layout-controller registration moves out of the controller files into a new `contrib/layout/browser/sessions.layout.contribution.ts`, which selects the desktop vs mobile controller per platform and registers the experimental setting. `sessions.desktop.main.ts` / `sessions.web.main.ts` now import the contribution.

## Tests

- 41/41 `LayoutController` unit tests pass, including the existing D7 cases and two new navigation guards (aux-bar side-panel reveal and working-set editor reveal). Both guards were verified to fail when the fix is neutralized.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run valid-layers-check` are clean.

Specs updated: `LAYOUT_CONTROLLER.md`, `desktopSessionLayoutController.md`, plus a Common Pitfalls entry in the sessions SKILL.

This request is not asking to change the Agent Host implementation. It is asking to make the existing `/code-review` command discoverable and usable through the normal Claude Code chat-session command contribution path as well.

title: Agents mobile: find known workspaces by name in the workspace picker
body: ## Problem The mobile workspace picker uses host listFolders for inline folder search. That contract is path-prefix based, so typing a bare nested repo name from the default directory can show no folder matches even when the repo is already known from recent workspaces. ## Chosen fix This stacks on PR #322812 and is part of the Agents mobile UX series. The fix is client-side and additive: while preserving the existing host folder browsing flow, the mobile sheet also matches recent/known workspace rows by label and description and shows those matches in a Recent section above folder results. PR3's explicit Open this folder confirm row remains in place for folder browsing. ## Out of scope Fully recursive or fuzzy host search is intentionally out of scope. Host listFolders remains path-prefix based and still supports drill-down by paths such as Projects/. ## Verification - [x] npm run typecheck-client - [x] npm run valid-layers-check - [x] Council review: no blocking issues found - [ ] npm run precommit / scripts/test.sh --grep WorkspacePicker could not complete in this worktree because the shared node_modules symlink is missing gulp-merge-json; no npm install performed per task constraints. --- ## ✅ On-device verification (iOS Simulator) Verified on an **iPhone 17 (iOS 26.4) Simulator** in mobile Safari, running a build of this branch, **signed in with a real GitHub account** and connected to a **real agent host** (the `osvaldos-macbook-pro` tunnel) — real filesystem browsing, real auth, **no mocks**. **Match known workspaces by name** _Typing a name evaluates the new recent-workspace match section. Here it shows the host-accurate **"No recent workspaces or folders match"** empty state (the typed name has no recent workspace on this host), confirming the matching path is wired up and active._

title: Agents mobile: prevent accidental workspace-group collapse
body:
## Issue
In the Agents window sessions list, sessions are grouped by workspace under a collapsible header. On **touch/phone** the entire header row toggled collapse, so a tap meant to open the **first session** frequently collapsed the whole workspace group instead (observed on a real iPhone). The collapse target overlapped the first session row.

## Fix (phone-gated behavior + a11y)
- The section/group **chevron is now a real `<button>`** (`type=button`) with `aria-expanded` and an `Expand/Collapse {name}` `aria-label`, focusable and keyboard-toggleable (previously an `aria-hidden` span).
- On phone layout, the tree uses **`expandOnlyOnTwistieClick`** for session sections/groups, so the **row body no longer toggles collapse** — only the chevron does. Desktop keeps honoring `workbench.tree.expandMode` (unchanged).
- Chevron taps go through a shared toggle helper that **stops propagation**, so row selection/open is unaffected.
- CSS: chevron button styling + a `:focus-visible` outline using `--vscode-*` tokens; the collapsible chevron is always visible on phone.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- [ ] On-device: tapping a group's first session opens it; only the chevron collapses the group; chevron is keyboard/screen-reader accessible.

> Part of a series of Agents-window mobile UX fixes (separate PRs).
